paper.title: Towards Long-horizon Embodied Agents with Tool-Aligned Vision-Language-Action Models
paper.central_claim: A VLM planner can orchestrate diverse bounded VLA tools with typed family calls and progress-driven replanning, while invocation-aligned post-training and family residual adapters make those tools instruction-faithful, improving long-horizon manipulation in simulation and on a real robot under matched data and compute.

sections_read: All supplied text L1-L48: Abstract, Sections1-6 and Appendices A-G

evidence.support_explanation: Original proposal trains tool executors to follow typed agent invocations, not merely a planner wrapped around frozen original VLA.
Distinct adapters route execution by callable family; shared VLA and local instructions form the executor interface.
For pi05, adding a plain planner worsens both LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin; this is not a cost-free hierarchy benefit.
TAPT+typed interface improves pi05 over standalone; reported simulator success, not our execution.
Per-task physical success counts with common initial configurations and hardware. Long task improvement is smaller.

evidence.quote: Both use 30 demonstrations per task, 30K training steps on eight A100s, one RTX 4090 at inference, and the same 20 marked initial configurations.
evidence.support_explanation: Real comparator equalizes demos, optimizer steps, inference GPU and initial configurations, but not all planner monetary costs.
Table4 is a cumulative training stack plus interface-only/full endpoints. It does not isolate all interactions or progress-monitor causality.

evidence.quote: we supervise a scalar progress signal using a normalized temporal proxy.
evidence.support_explanation: Training target measures execution-window time, not independently calibrated semantic completion.
Progress triggers handoff, and stagnation triggers replanning; qualitative success/failure traces are not a detector confusion matrix.

evidence.quote: global video understanding, state-change-based segmentation, and definition-conditioned tool-family labeling.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline training labels can use future/global video and robot-state transitions; do not assume deployment receives this privileged future context.
RL subtask rewards and boundary resets use simulator-state truth; deployment relies on learned progress, not these oracle predicates.

evidence.quote: after Stage 3, end-to-end fine-tuning retains 86.4% of prior skills, while ours retains 97.6% and achieves 95.0% final LIBERO-Long success
evidence.support_explanation: Independent staged offline expansion tests retention with new family demonstrations; not autonomous self-improvement.

evidence.quote: Adapters add only 9% parameters and 7% inference time to OpenVLA-OFT
evidence.support_explanation: Local adapter overhead measured relative to backbone; total agent cost not inferred from this alone.

evidence.quote: The call counts measure VLM requests during execution and exclude initial plan construction
evidence.support_explanation: Measured reductions omit initial planning, so cannot be read as total agent call count.
Event-triggered vs periodic monitoring reduces execution-time VLM queries for three executors; budget asymmetry and full wall time need audit.

evidence.quote: we use CALVIN_D and split episodes into 80% training and 20% testing.
evidence.support_explanation: Within-D episode split is not standard cross-environment ABC-to-D transfer.

evidence.quote: all methods compared within the same benchmark use the same held-out tasks, initial-state files, rollout horizons, random seeds, and success predicates.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched native environment success and many trials, but harness design/tuning disjointness is not established by test naming.

evidence.quote: We pre-sample and physically mark 20 randomized initial object configurations, and use the same configurations for both methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Paired configurations and final-state task definitions support real deployment measurement; no run-to-run statistical inference is reported.

signatures.object: Agent-callable VLA executor stack; replaces monolithic task command or direct planner wrapping
signatures.information: Planner sees task/scene/history; tool receives local scene-grounded instruction and family ID. Training labels use global demonstrations and simulator boundary/reward state; no evidence that future trajectory context is supplied at deployment.
signatures.operation: VLM emits typed (family, local instruction) sequence; shared VLA routes through family LoRA; bounded action/progress rollout; completion hands back, stalled progress invokes replanning.
signatures.output: Physical actions, temporal progress estimates, and revised tool sequence
signatures.conditions: Tool registry covers required primitives; segmentation/labels correspond to invoked semantics; normalized temporal proxy must generalize to actual failures.
signatures.feedback: 2Hz action/progress inference; threshold0.90 and stagnation windows, supplemented by VLM scene reasoning on intervention.
signatures.selection_rule: Runtime fixed threshold and stagnation; not test-set optimization of a persistent harness.
signatures.selection_data: Progress targets from segmented training clips; local RL uses oracle simulator predicates and refreshed boundary reset pools.
signatures.persistence: Offline IA SFT/post-training and family adapters stored as policy weights; no per-episode retained harness modifications.
signatures.later_use: Same interface and trained family tools used for later benchmark rollouts and paired physical task trials.
signatures.failure_boundary: Out-of-registry actions require more demos; temporal progress can diverge from physical completion; handoff distribution shift and cumulative-component confounds remain.

signatures.object: Staged offline addition of pull and push families
signatures.information: New-operation demonstrations plus frozen shared backbone and earlier family adapters.
signatures.operation: Train only newly added family adapter; keep old adapters fixed; evaluate preceding skills after each stage.
signatures.conditions: New skill expressible with family adapter and same backbone; demonstrations needed.
signatures.feedback: Held earlier-skill success and final LIBERO-Long success; not online autonomous acceptance.
signatures.selection_rule: Predetermined family expansion/training, not a search-and-select self-optimization algorithm.
signatures.selection_data: Training demos for newly added operations; test earlier families separately.
signatures.persistence: Frozen prior adapters and new adapter weights.
signatures.later_use: Stage3 retained-skill evaluation and final benchmark suite.
signatures.claimed_effect: 97.6% prior retention versus86.4% end-to-end;95% final suite.
signatures.failure_boundary: One staged simulation experiment does not establish unlimited skill growth, new embodiments or autonomous discovery.

gap.author_gap: Long-horizon planners can reason but VLA executors lack stable callable invocation semantics and trustworthy handoff/progress interfaces; plain wrapping can conflict with a monolithic policy.
gap.checked_gap: Direct planner drops pi05 LIBERO92.4→80.4 and RoboTwin39.38→30.0, substantiating a concrete interface mismatch. Success improves after both interface and training changes, not after orchestration alone.

claims.text: Typed callable tools and TAPT improve long-horizon task completion.
claims.setting: LIBERO-Long, selected single-arm RoboTwin, CALVIN_D and two longer-horizon benchmarks
claims.baseline/control: Standalone SFT VLA, direct planner using SFT tools, full aligned executor/interface; OpenVLA/OFT/pi05.
claims.selection_vs_test: Downstream training is benchmark-specific; CALVIN80/20 episodes. Test splits/horizons/seeds shared, but not proof of no harness-development overlap.
claims.result/denominator: pi05 LIBERO92.4→97.2, RT39.38→62.50; LIBERO50 rollouts/task, RT8 tasks×20. RoboMem26×10, RoboLab120×5.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported benchmark gains of combined trained interface/tool system, not orchestration alone or calibrated semantic verification.

claims.setting: One FrankaFR3, one front D435; Simple/Conditioned/Long tasks
claims.baseline/control: Fine-tuned pi05 versus complete system, same30 demos/task,30K steps,eightA100,4090 and20 marked starts.
claims.selection_vs_test: Evaluation marked initial layouts; same tasks receive training demonstrations; no unseen embodiment or untouched scene set proven.
counterevidence: Single robot/camera; heterogeneous task gains, no paired outcome table/CI.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Local counted real closed-loop improvement, not general sim-to-real transfer.

claims.text: Progress-triggered invocation improves planner efficiency and family adapters preserve old skills.
claims.setting: Runtime query ablation and separate staged offline expansion study
claims.baseline/control: Periodic VLM monitoring every5 steps; end-to-end continued training versus family-only expansion
claims.selection_vs_test: Runtime thresholds fixed; predetermined new-family training with prior-skill later evaluation. No autonomous retained harness search.
claims.result/denominator: pi05 execution calls57.2→0.228 excluding initial plan;97.6% vs86.4% prior-skill retention after stage3.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reduced execution monitoring calls and scoped offline skill retention, not full dollar efficiency or guaranteed completion detection.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported native-environment task success across several manipulation suites and counted real paired-start trials support the combined trained callable-tool system. Local progress is a temporal proxy, component effects are partly bundled and training covers the real task families. Transfer is not assigned solely for many benchmarks, CALVIN within-D holdout or real hardware: development-disjoint scene/embodiment evidence is insufficient.
unresolved: Completion confusion matrix under perturbation and independent progress contribution.
Full initial-plan+execution cost, failed-run usage and matched interaction budgets.
Development versus test-task overlap and repeated training-run/paired uncertainty.
